newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICN to buy out Hungarian small investors.
newsitem.headline: ICN to buy out Hungarian small investors.

text.p: U.S.-based ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc offered on Tuesday to buy out small shareholders of Hungarian drug company Alkaloida Rt in which it has a majority stake.
The offer is valid for stakes under one percent in the company and the offered price is 570 forints per share or 57 percent of the nominal value, ICN said in the official bourse gazette.
The buyout offer was part of the privatisation contract signed in 1996.
ICN bought a 50.02 percent share package worth a nominal 2.431 billion forints for $9.11 million or 57 percent of the nominal value last June.
It later raised the company's issued share capital to 6.96 billion forints in two steps, leaving the state privatisation agency APV Rt with a 25 percent plus one share stake.
Alkaloida Rt, based in Tiszavasvari, east Hungary, was granted a 35-year exclusive licence for the production of opium derivatives and psychotropic drugs in 1993.
